questions.q: What is Quick Additions designed for?
options: Highly unusual, one-off assets needing many overrides
Routine assets where category defaults are already correct
Assets that originate exclusively from Payables invoices
Assets being retired rather than added
questions.explain: Quick Additions is built for the majority of routine additions where the category's default depreciation rules are already correct, speeding up data entry.

questions.q: Which fields does Quick Additions actually require?
options: Depreciation method, life, and every GL account, entered manually
Description, category, cost, units, date placed in service, and book
Only the asset's physical location
An approved Payables invoice number
questions.explain: Quick Additions asks only for what can't be defaulted elsewhere; depreciation method, life, convention, and GL accounts come from the category book automatically.

questions.q: Why does Quick Additions depend more heavily on good category design than a manual addition does?
options: Because its defaulted fields aren't shown for per-asset review
Because it ignores category assignments entirely
Because Quick Additions always overrides category defaults
Because categories don't apply to Quick Additions at all
questions.explain: Since Quick Additions never displays the defaulted depreciation fields for confirmation, a poorly designed category can silently apply wrong defaults with no visible warning.

questions.q: Which of these scenarios requires going back to a manual Add Asset instead of Quick Additions?
options: Twelve identical laptops bought on the same day for the same cost center
An asset that needs to be split across multiple distributions at the point of addition
An asset whose category defaults are already correct
An asset placed in service on the first day of the fiscal year
questions.explain: Quick Additions does not support setting up multiple distributions at the point of addition, so that scenario requires the full manual Add Asset flow.

questions.q: What happens to the depreciation method and GL accounts during a Quick Addition?
options: They must be typed in manually on the Quick Additions screen
They are inherited from the category book with no per-field review on that screen
They are left blank until the first depreciation run
They default from the General Ledger calendar
questions.explain: Quick Additions pulls depreciation method, life, convention, and GL accounts directly from the category book without displaying them for individual confirmation.
